description: Sign-in required: call connect(email) and connect_verify first (free, one email) unless this connection is already signed in. Read a document by its own structure: give a pinpoint (straipsnis) like '6.38' for one article, or from_unit and count to page through it. On a ruling (nutartis / sprendimas), pass ruling_part=disposition to read only the operative order (rezoliucinė dalis). Never by character offset (read_source_text reads the publisher's text that way, without our structure). `document_id` is required and comes from a result: a search hit's `id` (an article id with `#` opens at that article) or `document.id`; a case number or an act number is not an id (find it with search_practice / search_law first). Page size is `count`; there is no `limit` or `max_chars` here. `paragraphs` contain the served text; inspect its `version`/`wording` qualifications before calling it current law. `on_date` requests separate `wording_on_date`, whose held/composed/missing evidence must support any historical claim. A # unit or pinpoint overrides `from_unit`. For whole-document paging, continue an unfiltered read as shown below. ECHR cases (`coe.hudoc:`) have no paragraphs here: the answer is the case card and its HUDOC link. Example arguments: {"document_id": "<document_id from search result>", "pinpoint": "6.217", "count": 1, "on_date": "2024-01-15"}. Replace the first bracketed document_id with the id returned by your search. To continue an unfiltered read, use its response document_id without a # fragment, set from_unit to its next_from_unit, omit pinpoint/article, and keep other filters. A next_from_unit from a pinpoint-filtered read is not a whole-document offset. Continuation arguments: {"document_id": "<document_id from previous read>", "from_unit": 14, "count": 3, "on_date": "2024-01-15"}.

article.description: Jump to an article by its number alone: `57`, `6.217`. Same effect as `pinpoint` with less typing — pass one or the other, not both naming different articles.
article.title: Article

count.description: How many paragraphs to return, default 5. With `pinpoint`/`article` and no count you get that provision's own paragraphs; with a count, the read opens at the provision and reads on in document order (`pinpoint='31 p.', count=3` gives paragraphs 31-33). The Civil Code runs to 1.7 million characters, so read in pages rather than asking for everything.
count.title: Count

document_id.description: What to read: the `id` of a search hit - an article id (containing `#`) opens at that article and reads on - or the whole document's id to start at the top.
document_id.title: Document Id

from_unit.description: One-based position for a read without `pinpoint`/`article`, using the response's `document_id` without a `#` fragment. A `#` unit or pinpoint overrides it. Continue an unfiltered read with `next_from_unit`; that value from a pinpoint-filtered read is not a whole-document offset. There is no cursor.
from_unit.title: From Unit

jurisdiction.description: Which jurisdiction the id belongs to (`LT`). Omit for the account's own.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

lang.description: Which language version to read, as a two-letter code (`lt`, `en`, `fr`), for a document held in several languages; `<id>@en` in `document_id` does the same. Omit for the default version: Lithuanian where held, else the source language. Pinpoints are the same in every language; the answer names the language served and the others held.
lang.title: Lang

on_date.description: On an act's article: `YYYY-MM-DD` requests separate `wording_on_date`, with its edition window, link and held/composed/missing qualification. Passing the date does not make `paragraphs` historical: they contain the text served by this read. Inspect `version` and `wording` qualifications before treating that text as current law. Use the separate dated result only to the extent its evidence supports it.
on_date.title: On Date

pinpoint.description: Jump to a location by name, as a lawyer writes it: `6.217 straipsnis`, `13 straipsnis. 2 dalis`. Omit when the id already names the place.
pinpoint.title: Pinpoint

ruling_part.description: On a ruling only: return paragraphs from one section — `recital` (case history and parties' arguments under nustatė), `reasoning` (konstatuoja) or `disposition` (nutaria — the operative order). Omit for statutes.
ruling_part.title: Ruling Part

section.description: On a ruling only: the numbered section(s) the court prints - `IV` for section IV, `IV+` (or `nuo IV`) for it and every later one. Combines with ruling_part: ruling_part=`reasoning`, section=`IV+` reads only the court's reasoning from section IV on, in one call.
section.title: Section

session.description: The `session` value the sign-in returned. Pass it on every call in this conversation, so the sign-in survives however this client handles connections; omit it when the user connected with Sign in (OAuth) or a key.

voice.description: On a ruling only: return only the paragraphs in this voice - `court` (the court alone speaking, including its restatements of earlier rulings; `court_own` without them; `court_interpretation` its interpretation only), `party` (a party's argument or the question its appeal raises), `lower_court`, `institution`, `opinion`, or one voice name. Every paragraph of a ruling carries `voice` either way; a paragraph with more than one speaker is `mixed`, with each fragment's voice.
voice.title: Voice

name: read_paragraphs
title: Read a provision or paragraphs
